source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

Its fallback is truncated and access assumptions are unapproved.

Given the adjacent GB_HSC sensor family and power-platform naming, V3.1 treats HSC as presumptive hot-swap controller, subject to Project confirmation, and requires the exact power device/rail and management path rather than connector semantics.

original_test_intent: Verify `TEMP_STBY_HSC`—presumptively the standby-domain hot-swap controller temperature—is readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with the correct component/rail identity, value, units, status and supported thresholds for the approved platform and current power state.
original_method: Confirm the HSC meaning, resolve the stable BMC record and exact standby hot-swap controller or other Project-defined component, bind it to its board location, power rail/domain and management path, then compare complete passive raw/UI fields with state-specific limits under the existing AC/host power and standby load. Preserve logs and do not change power state.
manual_activity: The platform owner defines HSC, identifies the standby power controller/rail and telemetry path, and supplies the expected reading or unavailable state for the current AC/host power condition. Automation can collect the record and both UI views; a human resolves acronym/power-domain ambiguity and owns the verdict. No power transition or load/fault stimulus is authorized.
required_inputs: Project definition of HSC and exact chassis/board/BMC/BIOS plus standby controller PN/revision and physical location
Standby rail/domain, source/load path and controller relationship to AC presence and host G3/S5/S0 states
BMC management controller/bus/mux/address and exact die/internal/external temperature field
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health rows
State-specific units, scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health, unavailable/zero and freshness semantics
Recorded AC presence, host/chassis power state, standby current/load, fan mode/speeds, airflow and timestamp alignment
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, protected authentication and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL or system logs; power-domain, hot-swap-controller, standby and thermal events are essential context.

Do not expand HSC as high-speed connector or hot-swap controller solely from the acronym. Confirm the Project component; until then, retain the likely hot-swap interpretation as a review hypothesis only.

Do not change AC or host power state, cycle the chassis, switch rails, alter standby load, inject overcurrent/thermal faults or modify controller limits. Record the existing state for this passive row.
Treat I2C/I3C/management access as BMC/platform scope. Require controller/bus/mux/address and exact field; host power-state information alone cannot prove the BMC sensor source.

Apply the approved state matrix: unavailable or different values in G3/S5/S0 may be valid. A readable number in the wrong power state does not establish coverage, and absence is not automatically FAIL.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable Script. Stop without automatic retry on ambiguous component/rail, stale data or raw/UI/state disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, HSC definition, standby controller/rail/management topology, current power state, client and Script; establish the state-specific expected record before collection.
Capture the complete raw/API record and unchanged Dashboard plus Server Health rows with identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamps.
Record AC/host state, standby load/current and cooling context, then compare only with the approved matching state specification and any equivalent controller telemetry.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, power transition/cycle, load/fault stimulus, rail/controller/fan/threshold change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Confirm the authoritative HSC expansion and exact standby component, rail/domain, physical location and BMC management source.
Provide the G3/S5/S0 or Project-specific availability/value/threshold/status/freshness matrix and approve the tool/Script.
Review the passive evidence under the documented power state and issue the formal verdict without demanding a power transition or importing connector semantics.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The literal query can retrieve a record if the name is exact, but it cannot establish HSC meaning, component/rail/management identity, power-state applicability or UI/spec agreement. The fallback is truncated, and the command exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Resolve TEMP_STBY_HSC through complete inventory and the approved standby controller/rail map, retrieve it with protected read-only access under the current documented power state, and correlate both UI paths with the state-specific specification without changing power.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_STBY_HSC, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review adds acronym/power-state controls without editing Master or cycling power.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the stable BMC sensor to the exact standby hot-swap controller or Project-defined HSC component, power rail/domain and management bus, record the current AC/host/standby-load state, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with the matching state-specific acceptance matrix.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact board, standby power architecture and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board/controller revision, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, power-state policy, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Standby power schematic and HSC component map, BMC management-bus/sensor definition, controller thermal limits, power-state behavior, WebUI schema and Project specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the ambiguous HSC target, binds it to a power domain and applies state-specific availability/limits while preserving the passive display check.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A passive reading in one existing power state does not validate hot-swap function, inrush/current limiting, fault response, other power states, cycling, alarms or protection behavior; those require separate approved tests.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: HSC component/rail/bus map, state-specific acceptance, current standby load/cooling context, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The acronym is vendor-specific; standby devices can remain powered when the host is off, sensor availability can change by state, and UI polling may lag transitions even though no transition is performed here.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or controller telemetry as an approved alternative to ipmitool only with the original method preserved, interface/version/field and reason recorded, engineer approval and equivalent component/rail identity, power-state context, value, threshold, status and freshness evidence. Connector temperature or a generic standby rail value is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Project-approved HSC definition; chassis/board/BMC/BIOS and standby controller PN/revision/location plus rail/domain/load-path identity
BMC controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature-field source
Current AC presence and host/chassis state, standby current/load and fan/airflow context with timestamps
Complete raw/API record with stable ID, value, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamp
Redacted Dashboard and Server Health evidence mapped to the same component and state-specific specification comparison
Pinned Script/tool security evidence, no-clear/no-power-change/no-load-or-fault/no-write/no-retry proof, final power/BMC health, limitations and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: HSC is underdefined, but Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently request passive validation of one named standby temperature record. The Project can resolve whether HSC is the likely hot-swap controller and supply state-specific acceptance, so this is readiness uncertainty rather than an irreducible conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target record and passive state-aware thermal purpose are identifiable. Component/rail semantics and expected power-state behavior can be supplied by the Project, so missing inputs do not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains hybrid classification and state-awareness but corrects the unsupported `high-speed connector` expansion to a Project-confirmed, presumptive hot-swap-controller interpretation based on the sensor family.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence reasoning with acronym/component, rail/domain, management-source and power-state-specific evidence.

review_improvement: Prevents a standby hot-swap-controller sensor from being misreviewed as a connector temperature, prevents wrong-state absence from being called a failure and prevents power cycling or fault injection from being added to a passive display case.
independent_technical_reasoning: In server power platforms, HSC commonly means hot-swap controller, and the adjacent `GB_HSC1~10` family makes that more plausible than high-speed connector, though Project confirmation remains mandatory. A standby controller can stay active across selected host-off states, so acceptance must be tied to AC and host power context. This row observes telemetry only and provides no authority to exercise inrush, faults or state transitions.
